map.埃特巴什码（Atbash cipher）是一种已知最早的替换密码之一，起源于希伯: The Atbash cipher is one of the earliest known substitution ciphers, originating in Hebrew. Its name comes from the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, Aleph, the second, Beth, the second-to-last, Taw, and the last, Shin — Aleph-Taw, Beth-Shin, hence Atbash.
map.埃特巴什码将字母表反转，使第一个字母与最后一个字母对应，第二个与倒数第二个对应，: Atbash reverses the alphabet so that the first letter maps to the last, the second to the second-to-last, and so on:
f(x) = 25 − x  (where x is the letter position, A=0, B=1, ... Z=25)
map.（involution），也就是说加密和解密使用完全相同的操作。对明文应用一次埃: — encryption and decryption use exactly the same operation. Apply Atbash once to the plaintext to get the ciphertext, then apply it once more to recover the plaintext.
This is because reversing the alphabet twice restores the original order: A→Z→A, B→Y→B, ...
map.埃特巴什密码最早出现在《耶利米书》中，用希伯来语书写。它被用来掩盖一些地名和人名: The Atbash cipher appears as early as the Book of Jeremiah, written in Hebrew. It was used to conceal place names and personal names — for example "Babylon" was written as "Sheshach". It also appears in medieval Jewish mystical literature.
map.埃特巴什码的安全性极低，因为它只有一种固定的替换方式，不需要密钥。任何人只要知道: Atbash offers extremely weak security because it uses only one fixed substitution and requires no key. Anyone who knows it is Atbash can decrypt it immediately. For the 26-letter alphabet it is essentially a special case of the Caesar cipher with a shift of 13.
